clinician.trajectory_summary: An 87-year-old male with long-standing hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and prior lung cancer presented in November 2020 with anorexia, nausea, and acute-on-chronic kidney injury (serum creatinine 428 μmol/L from baseline ~187 μmol/L). Workup revealed proteinuria (2.38 g/24h), hypocomplementemia (C3 0.53 g/L), elevated serum IgG (25.65 g/L), peripheral eosinophilia (0.73 × 10^9/L), elevated total IgE (453.3 IU/mL), generalized superficial lymphadenopathy, and a right lower ureter mass causing hydronephrosis. Ureteroscopy with biopsy and double-J stent placement was performed. Histopathology of the ureteral mass demonstrated fibrous tissue with IgG4-positive plasma cells. Kidney biopsy confirmed IgG4-TIN with >25 IgG4+ plasma cells per high-power field, IgG4/IgG ratio of 35%, and storiform fibrosis, alongside diabetic glomerulosclerosis changes. Serum IgG4 was markedly elevated at 1890 mg/dL. Following stent placement, creatinine improved to 279 μmol/L. Treatment with methylprednisolone 32 mg/day (tapered to 16 mg/day after 5 weeks, then 4 mg/day by one year) resulted in resolution of lymphadenopathy, ureteral mass, and hydronephrosis by one-year follow-up, with creatinine stabilizing around 200 μmol/L and IgG4 normalizing to 59 mg/dL.
